patient_overview.name: Gayle Rowe
patient_overview.description: Gayle Rowe is a 53-year-old man in Cliffside Park, New Jersey, living with his wife and extended family of six, who comes in juggling hypertension, prediabetes, kidney and heart disease, and a mouth still healing from recent dental work. He speaks in short bursts, often trailing off and needing a question asked twice before he answers fully, and he visibly loses track of what he was saying. He knows his doctor wants him to change how he eats but feels buried under pill bottles, appointments, and a diet plan he found on a wellness page a neighbor shared with him. His wife, who is anxious and watchful, usually sits close by and jumps in to fill gaps in his answers.

demographics.occupation: Former warehouse inventory clerk, now not working due to disability
demographics.residence: Cliffside Park, New Jersey; household of 6
demographics.cultural_context: Gayle grew up in a working-class household in northern New Jersey where big Sunday dinners were the one time the whole family sat down together, a habit he still misses now that chewing is hard and money is tight. He takes pride in having gone further in school than his parents did, but says numbers and medical words "swim" for him, and he relies on his wife or his phone to explain things back to him in plain terms.

nutrition_profile.dietary_pattern: A loosely followed 'clean eating' plan he saw shared on social media by a neighbor, built around smoothies, avoiding anything labeled sugar, and cutting out most bread, though he doesn't follow it consistently
food_preferences: Soft foods now because of his mouth, like mashed potatoes and oatmeal
Canned soups he can heat up fast
Deli turkey sandwiches when his teeth allow it
foods_or_behaviors_to_explore: How much sodium is in the canned soups and deli meats he leans on
Portion sizes and timing of meals relative to insulin dosing
Hidden sugar in flavored protein powders he adds to smoothies
How often he eats out of boredom or stress versus hunger
nutrition_profile.meal_pattern: Irregular; sometimes skips breakfast, grazes through the day, then a large dinner with the household
nutrition_profile.hydration: Drinks mostly water during the day but says little about evening drinks
nutrition_profile.physical_activity: Mostly sedentary; short walks around the block a few times a week when he feels up to it
nutrition_profile.substance_use: Reports drinking 'just a beer or two' on weekends but minimizes further detail
nutrition_profile.sleep: Fragmented sleep, waking several times a night, sometimes due to needing the bathroom

psychosocial_profile.personality: Overwhelmed and scattered, easily loses the thread of a conversation, seems to be carrying too many instructions at once
psychosocial_profile.communication_style: Gives short, clipped answers at first; opens up more if a question is gently repeated or rephrased a second time
goals: Keep his teeth situation from getting worse
Avoid needing dialysis down the line
Have enough energy to help his grandkids with homework
concerns: Confused about which foods are actually bad for his kidneys versus his blood sugar
Worried the dental work means he can't eat like he used to
Feels like there are too many diets and rules to keep track of
beliefs: Thinks 'natural' and 'sugar-free' labels mean a food is automatically fine for him
Believes his smoothie diet is healthy because a lot of people online use it
Thinks skipping a pill once in a while 'balances out' if he eats better that day
motivations: Wanting to still be around for his grandchildren
Not wanting his wife to worry more than she already does
Avoiding another hospital stay like the sepsis scare years back
fears: Having a heart attack like the ones his imaging keeps hinting at
Losing more teeth and not being able to eat with the family
barriers: Low health literacy makes instructions hard to retain
Household stress and crowding make quiet meal planning hard
Limited income relative to a household of six
Mouth pain limits what he can actually chew
strengths: Genuinely wants to do better for his family
Willing to try structured plans if explained simply
Has a partner who helps him remember appointments
psychosocial_profile.support_system: Wife is present and attentive but anxious, often answering for him or hovering nearby during visits, which sometimes helps and sometimes adds pressure
psychosocial_profile.readiness_to_change: Contemplation; aware something needs to shift but torn between wanting to stick with his social-media diet and the recommendations which hasn't been feeling results.
